sentences.text: Stand, gate, and passenger connection recovery begins after surface constraints have been reduced enough for individual aircraft rotations to become the controlling problem.

The Gate Conflict Detector compares planned arrivals, planned departures, assigned gates, towing availability, and published stand status to identify conflicts that would otherwise be hidden inside local spreadsheets.

The Ramp Movement Board maintains the operational view of occupied, blocked, cleaning, boarding, and tow-ready positions so that ramp decisions are based on the same stand timeline used by airport and airline users.
The Airport CDM Portal presents each gate conflict with the affected flights, passenger connection exposure, aircraft size compatibility, and the latest feasible off-block time.

The Airport Duty Manager sets the recovery priority for stands that can be reopened quickly, giving preference to positions that remove multiple downstream conflicts rather than a single isolated delay.
Airline Operations Coordinator uses the Gate Reopening Memo to confirm when a previously unavailable gate can be planned again for arrival handling, boarding, and connection recovery.
The Ramp Control Lead coordinates stand reopening with the Ground Handling Dispatcher so that ground equipment, marshalling staff, and safe access routes are available before a flight is reassigned.
The Surface Surveillance Adapter verifies that the apron position is physically clear, while the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor provide supporting movement evidence for the reopened area.
The Tower Supervisor is advised only when the gate or stand decision changes runway sequence assumptions, expected taxi duration, or a departure metering commitment.

The Aircraft Operator Representative confirms whether the aircraft can accept a revised stand assignment without disrupting maintenance release, fueling sequence, boarding control, or cabin readiness.

The Handling Resource Planner estimates whether the proposed turnaround can be recovered using available loading teams, passenger stairs, boarding bridges, cleaning crews, and baggage transfer resources.
The Airline Interface Adapter maintains airline-provided connection exposure, including protected passengers, minimum connection time pressure, and groups that require assisted transfer.
The Regional Flow Manager balances passenger connection pressure against network fairness when a gate recovery action would improve one bank of departures but consume scarce apron capacity.
The Network Operations Liaison reviews whether protecting a connecting passenger group supports wider network recovery or only transfers delay to a later sector.
The Slot Coordinator protects constrained rotations by checking that a recovered gate plan remains compatible with the applicable Calculated Takeoff Time and any slot compliance expectation.
The Target Off Block Time is revised only when the actor responsible for the turnaround confirms that the boarding, servicing, and ramp movement assumptions are achievable.
The Departure Metering Service sequences recovered departures so that aircraft released from delayed turnarounds do not create a new surface queue at the runway holding points.
Sector Load Monitor produces the Departure Fix Load Sheet when projected recovered departures require a consolidated view of demand by departure fix.
The Airport CDM Portal shows downstream departure-fix pressure as contextual information for gate recovery decisions, without allowing the stand plan to override accepted airspace constraints.
The Business Rules Registry holds the local rules for connection protection, gate compatibility, towing priority, stand reopening approval, and minimum turnaround recovery margins.
The Collaborative Decision Log records each accepted conflict resolution with the chosen stand, rejected alternatives, affected passenger connections, and the rationale used by the responsible actor.
The Audit Event Ledger preserves the same decision history for later traceability, including manual overrides, timestamp corrections, and identity of the approving role.

The Performance Analytics Warehouse measures whether recovered gate assignments reduced missed connections, reduced secondary stand conflicts, and improved aircraft rotation stability during the Recovery Phase.

The Data Governance Steward ensures that passenger connection information used for prioritization is aggregated or role-restricted so that operational users see only the detail required for recovery decisions.
